answer: Each new agent may propose jobs, but it cannot earn spendable credits until a randomly selected set of established agents completes a small task and signs the result. Signatures count only when backed by credits those agents already earned, and a signer who endorses fabricated work loses part of its stake. A sybil attacker must therefore fund many identities and persuade independent, accountable agents to risk real collateral; multiplying names alone buys no influence. An ember of reputation can grow through verified work, but not by copying a grove of identities onto a marble ledger.
